title: Media and Representation: History and Theory
academic_group: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
description: This course reviews the history and theory of media in artistic and spatial representation. It covers the development of various media forms from the late 20th century to the present, including paper-based, screen-based, 3D, and immersive spatial representation. Students will gain knowledge of how representation formats evolve in accordance with new technology and social conditions. They will be engaged in discussions on how they affect our perception and creation of the urban environment.
outcome: After completing this course, students will be able to:1.    Describe major concepts in and development in media and representation and explain how they relate to changing social, cultural, and technological conditions.2.    Analyse how different representational forms shape perception, experience, and the communication of ideas in artistic and spatial contexts.3.    Compare historical and contemporary approaches to artistic and spatial representation using appropriate critical concepts and vocabulary.4.    Apply media and representation theory to case studies in art, design, architecture, communication, or digital culture.5.    Reflect on the ethical, cultural, and environmental implications of representation technologies in contemporary practice.

title: Creative Dialogue
academic_group: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
description: This course facilitates participatory dialogues with practitioners on arts, design, and technology. Through case studies, discussions, reflection and exchange, students will gain an understanding of how creative disciplines intersect with social and cultural contexts. The dialogues will focus on technology-enabled creative works across the fields of arts, media, theatre, and architecture, beyond their disciplinary boundaries. Students are expected to take an active role in designing and curating the conservation, and to reflect upon how it shapes contemporary life and environment.
outcome: After completing this course, students will be able to:1.    Comprehend key ideas and practices in arts, design, media, architecture, and related creative fields.2.    Critically examine creative work in relation to its social, cultural, historical, and technological context.3.    Engage thoughtfully in dialogue with practitioners and peers to draw informed observations and reflective insights.4.    Interpreted interdisciplinary creative ideas, processes, and narratives with openness and critical awareness, to reflect upon their own assumptions/positions and to situate them within a broader cultural landscape.5.    Synthesise course learning into reflective, analytical, and creative responses.

title: Technological Practices in Arts and Design
academic_group: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
description: This course provides students with foundational knowledge and hands-on experience in the application of technology in arts and design practice. Through workshops and prototyping, students will learn different digital media techniques and experiment with producing prototypes using methods introduced in the course. By engaging directly with technology in a guided process and peer discussions, students will develop insights on how technology transforms artistic expression and design practice, fostering awareness of sustainability, ethics, and collaboration in design practice.

title: Field Study in Arts Technology
academic_group: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
description: This course aims to broaden students’ perspectives through a field study focused on arts and technology, creative industries, and related institutions or sites. It combines thematic seminars, workshops, field research, documentation and report to cultivate their interests and analytical capacity. A different topic and destination will be selected each year to reflect current development in art/tech practice, where students will undertake a design research project that includes on-site observation and engagement with cultural professionals and institutions to connect classroom learning with real-world creative practice.

title: Arts Technology Project
academic_group: Sch of Arch & Sch of JL & Comm
description: This course is a capstone project where students are required to complete an original design/research project in arts and technology under the supervision of a faculty member. The requirements may include, but are not limited to, literature review, data collection and analysis, report writing, original design, multimedia production, and project presentation or exhibition. Upon completion of this course, students will be able to plan and execute a design project in arts technology and provide evidence of their creativity and problem-solving ability to address an art tech issue.
